memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When you enter the land and plant any kind of fruit tree, regard its fruit as forbidden. For three years you are to consider it forbidden; it must not be eaten. In the fourth year all its fruit will be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD. But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit. In this way your harvest will be increased. I am the LORD your God.'" - Lev 19:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Plant a fruit tree, and wait. Three years without eating from it. The fourth year's fruit belongs to God. Only in the fifth year do you eat.

Five years of patience before you taste anything.

There is agricultural wisdom in this — young trees grow stronger when not harvested early. But there is spiritual training too. Israel is being taught to wait, and to give God the first fruit before taking any for themselves.

We are not good at this. We want returns quickly. We plant something on Monday and are discouraged by Friday. We start praying for someone and give up within the month. We begin a new discipline and abandon it when nothing has visibly changed.

But most of what matters grows slowly. Character. Marriages. Children. A congregation. A reputation for integrity. The work of God in a human heart.

Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up (Gal 6:9). At the proper time — which is rarely our time.

And notice the promise attached: in this way your harvest will be increased. Patience is not lost time. It is what makes a genuine harvest possible.

What are you about to give up on that simply needs more years?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have you abandoned too early because results were slow?
2. Where is God teaching you patience right now?
3. What would it look like to give God the "fourth year" first?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me patience with slow things. Keep me from giving up too early, and help me offer You the first of whatever grows. Amen.
